evidence: Footer social links render with alt/link text pulled from image filenames rather than the platform name — the Facebook icon's accessible name is the literal string "facebook-black" while the others resolve to bare platform names with no indication these are social links.
user_impact: Screen reader users navigating by link list hear "facebook-black link" instead of a meaningful label, and cannot tell from the link list alone that these four items form a related social-media group.
recommended_fix: Set alt text to a consistent pattern such as "Facebook (opens in new window)" for every icon, and wrap the group in a <nav aria-label="Social media"> landmark.

wcag_reference: 2.4.4 Link Purpose in Context, 4.1.2 Name Role Value
evidence: Each carousel item (e.g. Books, Ebooks & Audiobooks, Magazines, DVDs) is rendered as two adjacent links with identical text and identical href — one wrapping the thumbnail image, one wrapping the caption — rather than a single combined link.
user_impact: Keyboard and screen reader users must tab through two identical stops per carousel item to reach the same destination, roughly doubling the number of tab stops needed to get past this section.
recommended_fix: Combine the image and caption into a single <a> element per item, or add aria-hidden="true" and tabindex="-1" to the image link so only one stop remains per item.

wcag_reference: 1.3.1 Info and Relationships, 2.4.6 Headings and Labels
evidence: Heading levels do not follow a predictable hierarchy: an <h1> is followed by several <h2>/<h3> promotional headings ("Start here", "Hone your craft", "Never miss a thing"), then a <h5> ("Footer Bar Menu") with no intervening <h4>, and no headings identify the mega-menu panels themselves.
user_impact: Screen reader users who navigate by heading list (a primary AT navigation strategy) get a structure that skips a level and doesn't reflect the page's actual visual sections, making it harder to jump directly to the section they want.
recommended_fix: Restructure headings so each subsection follows the next sequential level (h1 → h2 → h3) with no skipped levels
owner: and add a visually-hidden heading above each mega-menu panel.

page_or_component: Homepage stray text nodes near themed sections
evidence: Raw CSS color values (e.g. "rgb(0,0,0)", "rgb(118,58,199)", "rgba(255,255,255,0)") appear as literal readable text content directly in the page's accessible content stream, interleaved between section headings — consistent with color/style values that are not properly scoped out of the accessible name/content tree.
user_impact: Screen readers may announce nonsensical strings like "r g b 118 58 199" in the middle of otherwise meaningful content, which is confusing and breaks the reading flow for blind and low-vision screen reader users.
recommended_fix: Audit the templates generating these sections to ensure style/color values are only ever applied as CSS (inline style attributes or classes), never emitted as visible/readable text nodes; add automated regression tests (e.g. axe-core in CI) to catch stray text nodes like this before deploy.

page_or_component: Repeated ""Learn more"" links across homepage spotlight blocks
evidence: At least two separate spotlight blocks (the eLibrary/Libby promo and the Digital Studio promo) use the identical link text "Learn more" pointing to two different destinations (/elibrary and /digital-studio).
user_impact: Screen reader users who pull up a list of all links on the page (a common navigation shortcut) see multiple identical "Learn more" entries with no way to tell them apart or know which destination each one leads to.
recommended_fix: Make link text unique and descriptive per destination, e.g. "Learn more about the Libby app" and "Learn more about the Digital Studio", or add an aria-label that includes the specific topic.
